news.title: Morocco vs North Korea: How & When to Watch the U17 Women's World Cup Round of 16 Clash
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s U17 Women’s national team return to action today, Wednesday, October 28, as they take on heavyweights North Korea in a high-stakes Round of 16 clash at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Maâmora. Youness Rabie’s side enter the knockout phase determined to write a new chapter in Moroccan women's football history. Having reached the Round of 16 as one of the best third-placed teams, the host nation faces a familiar roadblock: the very same North Korean side that ended their tournament run at this exact stage last year before going on to lift the trophy. North Korea arrive in Maâmora as four-time world champions in this age category and clear tournament favorites.

news.title: India U15 team come from behind to claim 3-2 win over Trinidad and Tobago 3-2 in FIFA U15 World Cup
news.lede: India will now face Afghanistan in the quarter-finals for positions 81 to 88. India produced a strong second-half comeback to defeat Trinidad and Tobago 3-2 in the Round of 16 of the lower bracket in Tier C at the FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival Azerbaijan 2026 at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 8A in Baku on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Trailing 0-2 at half-time after goals from Jaylon Carrington (6’) and Djoshua Cyrus (18’), the Blue Colts responded through a Victor Lalawmpuia brace (23’, 25’) before R Lalremruatfela (29’) completed the turnaround. India will now face Afghanistan, who defeated Namibia 6-2, in the quarter-finals for positions 81 to 88, at 13:00 IST tomorrow.

news.title: Gianni Infantino critic quits over World Cup controversy in latest Fifa re-election twist
news.lede: Japan Football Association vice-president Takeshi Okada has stepped down from his role over controversies surrounding this year's Fifa World Cup. Okada's departure occurred just one week after the Asian Football Confederation officially endorsed Fifa president Gianni Infantino for re-election. The former Japan manager stated that recent governance actions surrounding the tournament significantly diverged from his personal convictions regarding sporting integrity. The resignation highlights internal divisions within the Asian football governing body despite its recent public show of support for Infantino.

news.title: Telford football referee returns from 'incredible' China tournament
news.lede: A young football referee who has just returned from officiating at a world schools tournament in China has said it was a "scary" but also "incredible" experience. Callum Oram, 18, has been refereeing for three years and hopes to make it his full time career. He spent 11 days working at the International School Sport Federation Football World Cup in Suzhou and made friends with other young referees from around the world. The Telford College student said he believed the tournament would be a valuable learning experience and would help him move ahead in the game.

news.title: FIFA politics around Infantino re-election push Japanese official to resign
news.lede: GENEVA (AP) — Two-time World Cup coach Takeshi Okada resigned as Japanese soccer federation vice president in protest at the politics around FIFA during Gianni Infantino's campaign to be re-elected. Japan's soccer body on Wednesday published Okada's resignation statement dated last Saturday — 24 hours after the Asian Football Confederation had performed a U-turn by publicly supporting Infantino, who seeks a fourth and final presidential term at an election in March. Infantino has faced a backlash since July over his failed World Cup sell-off plan and broader management style including ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, provoking a furor from soccer leaders in Europe, North America and — initially — in Asia.

news.title: Football: JFA VP Okada resigns over displeasure with FIFA, national body
news.lede: TOKYO - The Japan Football Association announced Wednesday that Vice President Takeshi Okada, a former manager of the men's national team, has resigned before the end of his term. Sources familiar with the matter said the 70-year-old, who stepped down on Saturday, departed due to dissatisfaction over several issues involving world ruling body FIFA at this summer's World Cup, as well as the JFA's response. "There was a significant gap between the handling of issues surrounding this World Cup and my own personal principles," Okada said in a statement released by the JFA. "As a sportsman, I could not accept this, which led to my decision to resign."

news.title: Japan football vice president Okada quits over FIFA World Cup decisions
news.lede: Takeshi Okada, vice president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), resigned on Wednesday, stating that the organization’s "series of responses" to recent World Cup controversies conflicted with his personal values. Okada, who led Japan as head coach at the 1998 and 2010 World Cups, stepped down a week after Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa declared the region's full support for Gianni Infantino’s FIFA re-election bid during a meeting in Tokyo. The AFC's endorsement marked a shift coming just weeks after joining European and North American governing bodies in criticizing Infantino over plans to open major FIFA competitions to private investors. Infantino continues to face pressure over governance decisions as continental associations debate his leadership tenure.
